messages:
Alex (Support): Hey team — incoming enterprise customer hit a flurry of 429s + very high p95 latency during a spike. They say it feels like we're throttling them even though quota looks fine. Posting logs they attached below.

Maya (CSE): Which account + what endpoint? Any repro steps from their side?

Alex (Support): Account: acme-llm-prod. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate (text gen). They sent ~200 r/s of short prompts for a 30s window, then dropped. Attached log snippet: 

```
2026-03-10T14:05:02Z INFO request id=xyz status=200 time_ms=12 cache=MISS
2026-03-10T14:05:02Z INFO request id=abc status=200 time_ms=9 cache=HIT
2026-03-10T14:05:03Z WARN request id=def status=429 error=quota_exceeded
2026-03-10T14:05:03Z WARN request id=ghi status=429 error=burst_throttle
2026-03-10T14:05:04Z INFO request id=jkl status=200 time_ms=180 cache=HIT
```

Alex (Support): They also pasted Console view showing spikes in queued requests around the same time, with a sudden jump in per-route queue depth.

Eve (Oncall): A couple quick hypotheses: 1) quota exhaustion at the shard/host level (not org-level); 2) batching interaction + KV cache hotkeying causing head-of-line waits; 3) fallback routing hitting a slower model variant. Any runtime context, Sam?

Sam (Eng Runtime): Thanks. From those logs this looks classic 'perceived throttling' caused by continuous batching + KV cache behavior. Short prompts => many requests are eligible to join the same batch window. When the KV cache produces a MISS for some requests, those requests take longer (model run) while other requests in the batch wait for the whole batch to finish. That can increase p95 and cause request queues to back up; when queues hit per-host burst limits, we emit 429s.

Sam (Eng Runtime): TL;DR: not a global quota hole, it's local throughput shaping + batching latency amplification.

Maya (CSE): Good explanation. Customer is worried it's an auth/quota bug. How can we repro locally to show them?

Sam (Eng Runtime): Repro steps I used: spawn 3 short-client workers and hammer the hosted endpoint with tiny payloads and no streaming, emulate KV cache misses for a minority of keys. Example curl loop: 

```bash
for i in {1..500}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"rwd-compact-1","input":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
  sleep 0.002
done
wait
```

Sam (Eng Runtime): If you want to simulate KV misses, set your client to include random prefixes that aren't cached. Watch the console for 'batch_wait_ms' spikes and per-host queue depth.

Alex (Support): For the customer, what mitigation steps can we offer immediately?

Sam (Eng Runtime): Immediate options: 
- Suggest they smooth the burst (small client-side token-bucket) so requests arrive at more steady rate.
- Turn off or reduce continuous batching window for that API key/route (if they control the client SDK): lower batch_wait_ms or set max_batch_size lower.
- Increase per-route reserved concurrency / bump dedicated capacity (if on Dedicated).
- On our side we can temporarily increase per-host burst credits for their org while we investigate.

Maya (CSE): Can we also recommend changing prompt shape? Longer prompts amortize batching overhead. For embed/rerank workflows, batching behaves differently, so we should confirm they aren't mixing short chat-style calls.

Alex (Support): Customer tried smoothing on their side and saw improvement but still some 429s at peak. They want us to adjust something server-side.

Sam (Eng Runtime): I can do two things: 1) check per-shard metrics for acme-llm-prod to confirm whether a small subset of hosts saturated; 2) temporarily disable continuous-batching for their key (short window) in the control plane for a 30m window to confirm improvement.

Eve (Oncall): @deploy-bot can you check recent rollout that touched batching heuristics? Also flag the shard metrics.

deploy-bot: Noted. No recent rollout touching batching heuristics in the last 24h. Created incident ticket #INC-2026-312 and posted graphs: https://infra.redwood/graphs/INC-2026-312

Sam (Eng Runtime): Looking at the shard, there are two hosts that spike in queue depth and CPU. They handle ~70% of traffic due to a recent routing imbalance. I'll rebalance and temporarily add burst credits for the org.

Alex (Support): Can you also capture a small HAR or sample trace we can send to the customer to prove it's queuing? They want something to show their infra team.

Sam (Eng Runtime): Yup — I'll grab a trace (x-request-id + batch metadata) and redacted logs. ETA 15m.

Maya (CSE): For the customer-facing note, recommend: smoothing, reduce batch window or max batch size, consider short-term capacity bump. Provide the trace we get.

Alex (Support): I'll relay. Customer asked if billing will reflect retries/429s — they worry about being charged for failed attempts.

Eve (Oncall): We bill only for completed tokens; 429'd requests don't bill. I'll confirm with billing but that's our default.

Alex (Support): Perfect. Will follow up with the trace + temporary config change result. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Sam (Eng Runtime): Follow-up: after rebalancing + credits, p95 dropped ~45% in the repro window and 429s disappeared. I'll keep the temporary bump for 2 hours while we schedule a longer-term routing fix.

Maya (CSE): Great. I'll coordinate the long-term capacity plan with the account team.

Alex (Support): Closing loop with the customer now.

Eve (Oncall): Marking as resolved in the incident ticket for now, will reopen if they see more. :eyes:
